LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: DIRECT AND INDIRECT SPEECH

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we report what others have said?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech
2. apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: DIRECT AND INDIRECT SPEECH
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: DIRECT AND INDIRECT SPEECH
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech

What this means
In this part you learn to use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech to a partner. (skill: apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech.
3. Practise this skill: apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we report what others have said?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech.
5. Be able to: apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
